t.d: Hand rolling of premium cigars by torcedores from tobacco grown in the Vuelta Abajo.
t.tech: Hand rolling (totalmente a mano) by torcedores, mostly women today
t.mat: Tobacco from Vuelta Abajo and Semi Vuelta, Pinar del Río
t.auth: Boxes and labels carry 'Hecho en Cuba'; 'Totalmente a mano' marks fully handmade cigars.

t.d: Water-pipe smoking of sweetened muʽassel tobacco, called shisha in Egypt and arjīlah in the Levant.
t.auth: Sealed packs from named makers such as Al Fakher and Nakhla.

t.d: Clove-and-tobacco cigarettes first made in Kudus, credited to Hajj Djamhari, first sold as medicine.
t.tech: Tobacco blended with minced dried clove buds, hand-rolled or machine-made
t.auth: Crackling sound when burning; sold by named Indonesian makers.

t.d: Persian water pipe, with literary reference by Ahlī Shirazi before 1535 and a court post of hookah tender.
t.mat: Glass and precious metals for the rich

t.d: Moist steam-pasteurised tobacco placed under the upper lip, shifting from nasal snuff to snus by the early 1800s.
t.tech: Steam pasteurisation rather than fermentation; loose or portion
t.auth: Sold in Sweden under the EU exemption; most other EU sales of tobacco snus are banned.
